query: Explain how `hatch env lock`, implemented by `lock` in `src/hatch/cli/env/lock.py`, decides which environments to lock, and how the shared `run_lock_workflow` it hands off to treats incompatible environments, chooses where each lockfile is written, and behaves in check mode.

operations.name: The two export options are mutually exclusive
A named environment is expanded (a matrix name expands to its members)
With no arguments and nothing marked locked the command aborts
expressions: app.abort("No environments are configured with `locked = true`")

operations.name: An incompatible environment is skipped or aborts the run
The lockfile path is the export path, a per-environment file under the export-all directory, or the default

dependencies.name: Whether incompatible environments are tolerated depends on how the environment was selected and is passed down
An explicitly named environment that is not marked locked is refused unless an export option is given
expressions: if explicit_env is not None and not environment.locked and not export_path and not export_all_path:

dependencies.name: Environments that resolve to the same lockfile path are grouped and merged into one lock
expressions: environment, merged_deps, merged_extras, merged_groups, display_name = merge_environment_lock_inputs(

dependencies.name: In check mode a missing lockfile aborts; otherwise environments with nothing to lock are skipped with a warning
expressions: app.display_warning(f"Environment `{env}` has no dependencies to lock")
